newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans battle against monopolies in regions.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans battle against monopolies in regions.

text.p: Russia is taking its battle against monopoly behaviour into the regions with the formation of a new committee which first deputy premier Boris Nemtsov will probably head, a government official said on Wednesday.

Nemtsov, charged with monopoly reform in the government shakeup last month, told the cabinet that company managements who break anti-monopoly law should be held criminally liable in addition to company fines, Russian news agencies said.

He said reform of the so-called natural monopolies, as guided by a recent presidential decree, could generate 170 trillion roubles in federal budget revenues, they said. Russia describes big state-controlled companies in the electricity, gas and transport sector as natural monopolies.
The acting chairman of the anti-monopoly committee, Vadim Belov, told a news conference Nemtsov was slated to head a federal commission to coordinate anti-monopoly policy.
"This is not an increase in the anti-monopoly committee's powers, but it is a higher profile for anti-monopoly issues," he told Reuters.
Belov said the cabinet had also agreed to improve information gathering in the wholesale and consumer goods markets, where regions have put up trade barriers against each other.
But he said that heads of local governments had an unwelcome and strong influence on local monopoly committees.
"Many local heads have strong influence on (territorial) anti-monopoly committees, which of course makes it difficult to completely fulfil our duty."
He also said existing anti-monopoly regulation was not effective.
"In practice government regulation exists but the problem is the regulation is not effective," he said.

"On questions of monopolistic activity, for example, they refuse to come to agreements. When the natural monopolies refuse to come to agreement, we insist on them coming to agreement. There are a number of such instances."
